title: Number of 1 Bits
prompt:
Return the number of set bits (1s) in the binary representation of `n`. Treat `n` as a 32-bit value; negatives count their two's-complement bits.

**Example**: `11` (binary `1011`) → `3`; `-1` (all 32 bits set) → `32`.

Careful: a shift loop on a negative `n` needs thought (see the lesson).
hints: How can you inspect or remove one bit at a time, and what goes wrong with `n >>= 1` when n is negative?
`n & (n - 1)` erases the lowest set bit. Count how many times you can do that before n becomes 0. Loop on `n != 0`, not `n > 0`.
Alternative: check all 32 positions with `(n >>> i) & 1`. That is always 32 iterations with no sign issues.

solution.explanation: `n - 1` flips the lowest set bit and everything below it, so AND-ing with n erases exactly that bit. This works on the raw 32-bit pattern, so negatives are fine as long as the loop condition is `!= 0`. O(number of set bits) ≤ 32 iterations, O(1) space.
